case_number: Civil Appeal No. 14807 of 2024 (Arising out of SLP (C) No. 18977 of 2016)

parties.petitioner: Shri Mukund Bhavan Trust and Ors
parties.respondent: Shrimant Chhatrapati Udayan Raje Pratapsinh Maharaj Bhonsle and Another

summary: The appeal challenged the Bombay High Court's dismissal of a revision application, which concerned the trial court's refusal to reject a plaint under Order VII Rule 11(d) of CPC on grounds of limitation. The appellant Trust argued that the respondent's suit, seeking declaration of ownership, cancellation of compromise decrees, and possession of land, was barred by limitation under Articles 58, 59, and 65 of the Limitation Act, 1963. The respondent claimed a hereditary revenue grant (sanad) from 1710 and contended that the sale and compromise decrees concerning the land—executed without his knowledge—were invalid. The key issues were whether the cause of action was barred by limitation, whether the question of limitation could be decided at the plaint rejection stage, and whether the respondent had locus standi to challenge the decrees. The appellant contended the cause of action was illusory and time-barred, while the respondent asserted a fresh cause of action from 2007 upon discovering the alleged misconduct. The Court examined the nature of the Inam grant, adverse possession, and the validity of decrees dating back to the 1950s.
legal_provisions_cited: Order VII Rule 11(d) of the Civil Procedure Code, 1908
final_judgment: Pending final determination, leave granted; matter remanded for adjudication on merits regarding limitation and maintainability of the suit.
